system.summary: Meister key 65: letters as digit pairs, vowels as signs on a single digit, nulls 7 8 9 0, code letters and symbols for common words, three-digit codes for names; R5618 and R5620 use another system

diacritics.note: a vowel sign on a single digit: diaeresis a, circumflex e, bar i, cross o, small 2 u

system.sibling_key: targets/sega1590 and targets/sega1591b (the same key, Meister 1906 no. 65); used
system.notes: distinct_symbols counts the values of key/key.tsv that the decode uses with a sure value: 22 pairs, 5 vowel signs, 4 nulls, 21 code letters, 1 symbol (in) and 1 three-digit code (453). The doubtful con and the key's other symbols are left out. R5618 and R5620: key 65 gives .58 and .60 units with a value; no other key is known.

prior_solution.where: Decipherments of the time on f. 46r (R5613) and f. 230r (R5621). In this ledger: Brice Dudout read R5612 f. 17, R5616 f. 71 and R5615 in part (targets/sega1590, targets/sega1591b, 29 Oct 2026); George Lasry read the Paris copy of the letter of 9 Jan 1591 (targets/sega1591). No reading and no decipherment of the time gave a value of the decode.

solution.what: Transcription of the DECODE images of the 30 cipher pages of 9 records: 383 rows, 16,230 digit signs, 492 doubtful (TRANSCRIPTION.md).
Digit-pair counts of the pages, with no key: 24 pages form one group; R5618 and R5620 fall apart; four pages under 70 pairs cannot be placed (check.md, section 2).

Meister key 65, from this ledger's targets/sega1590/key.tsv, applied with the decode rules of key/README.md (scripts/decode.py) to 28 pages: .80 to .99 of the units of each of the 24 pages of the group have a value; R5618 .58 and R5620 .60 (check.md).

The decode against the decipherments of the time: R5621, 212 of 250 decode letters match f. 230r in order (.848); R5613, 121 of 144 match f. 46r (.840); with the pair values shuffled .172 and .138. A second measure on R5621, whose held-out test by Brice Dudout came before mine; this folder documents no held-out protocol of its own. scripts/check_decifrato.py gives these numbers from the rows and the clerk's lines in decifrato/; two label words of the transcription of f. 46r are outside the count (check.md, section 1).
No reading in sentences was made. The decode is not divided into words, so every document is decoded, not read.

outcome.method_basis: Meister's printed key no. 65 (1906), tied to Sega by George Lasry and given in targets/sega1590/key.tsv, applied with the decode rules of key/README.md; the text does not read as sentences in this folder.

texts.label: R5612, f. 17r, f. 17v, 26 November 1590
texts.summary: Sega on the imprisoned bishop, who leans to the opposite party (Navarre's); Sega will temporise. This agrees with Brice Dudout's reading; the decode shows parts of it.
texts.note: Decoded, not read; cipher words not counted. The record page gives the decode row by row, a summary and one doubt. It holds no reading in sentences.

texts.label: R5613, f. 45v, 9 January 1591
texts.summary: Lignerac goes, on the order of Umena (Mayenne), to Poitou and Brittany. This content comes from the decipherment of the time and from George Lasry's reading of the Paris copy.
texts.note: Decoded, not read; cipher words not counted. The record page gives the decode row by row, a summary and one doubt. It holds no reading in sentences.

texts.label: R5614, f. 47r, f. 48r, 9 January 1591
texts.summary: Words that seem to stand in the decode (my guess): confusion, the soldiery, discredit, the politiques, the death of a chevalier, a return, Saint-Denis.
texts.note: Decoded, not read; cipher words not counted. The record page gives the decode row by row, a summary and one doubt. It holds no reading in sentences.
